label: NEW PATTERNS

cover.headline: 4 signs you’re stuck *in a pattern*, not a problem
cover.sub: When the same moments keep going wrong.

points.heading: The same fight, different topic
points.body: Dishes, money, or plans, but it always ends the same way.
points.panel: “What do our arguments usually feel like, no matter the topic?”

points.heading: You can predict the next line
points.body: You both know the script before it starts.
points.panel: Notice the moment the script begins, and pause there.

points.heading: Fixing the topic doesn’t help
points.body: You solve one issue, and the feeling returns elsewhere.
points.panel: “Maybe it’s not about the dishes. Can we talk about what’s underneath?”

points.heading: You both feel unheard
points.body: Each of you is defending, and nobody feels understood.
points.panel: “I want to understand your side first.”

resource.name: Relationship Rewrite Method
resource.covers: Tools for looking at conflict, distance, and communication differently.

caption:
Sometimes the problem in a marriage isn’t the topic you argue about. It’s the pattern you both fall into every time.

Noticing the pattern is the first step to changing it. If you’d like tools for looking at conflict, distance, and communication differently, there’s a resource at the link in bio. It’s a place to start, and no resource can promise how another person will respond.

Follow @spotseason for more small steps.
